author: NorthEast News Desk
body: University of Rhode Island runner Lily Saul opened her 2026 cross-country season with a decisive individual victory at the Shawn M. Nassaney Invitational in Smithfield on Saturday morning. The fifth-year senior completed the 5-kilometer course in 17 minutes, 57.5 seconds and finished nearly 11 seconds ahead of Bryant’s Kelley Macelhiney in the 57-runner field.

Rhode Island placed four runners in the top 20. Zoe Catrambone finished 16th in 18:55.4, while Alison Pankowicz and Hailey LaRosa crossed in 18:55.8 and 18:56.4 to place 19th and 20th. Kelsey Wolff completed the Rams’ scoring group in 35th place at 19:46.3.

Host Bryant won the team competition with 33 points, followed by Merrimack with 52 and Stonehill with 61. URI placed fourth among five teams with 82 points. The result gave Saul an immediate individual benchmark after earning all-conference recognition last season. Rhode Island returns to competition September 19 at the UMass Dartmouth Invitational.
dek: The fifth-year senior won the 57-runner field by nearly 11 seconds as the Rams placed four runners in the top 20.
headline: Lily Saul wins Nassaney Invitational to open URI cross-country season
